summary: Frontend auth regression retest after cross-origin API base fix in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js. Tested on BOTH the alias hostname (llm-domain-metrics...) and the canonical hostname (723c8d12-...). All 6 requested flows PASS on both URLs: superadmin login, session persistence on reload, Domain Analysis navigation smoke, invalid-password specific error toast ('Invalid email or password'), and new-account registration ('Account created' toast, lands on /app). No 'Something went wrong' generic toast observed for any valid flow.
critical_code_review_comments: api.js same-origin fallback is correct and minimal; consider logging the resolved API base once for easier future debugging.
The recurring 401 console noise from /api/auth/me on unauthenticated pages is expected but could be suppressed by only calling /me when a session hint exists.
seed_data_creation: Created two throwaway registered users: qa+ppk526gk@test.com and qa+u8ze8s8l@test.com (password Test@1234) — safe to purge.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Cross-origin auth cookie bug is resolved by same-origin fallback in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js. When user opens alias URL, API base becomes window.location.origin, so httpOnly cookies work. Both alias and canonical URLs behave identically for login/register/session/refresh/invalid-pw/domain-analysis nav.
rca of the issue: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL pointed to canonical hostname while users opened the app via alias hostname. Cross-origin credentialed axios requests were blocked (ACAO wildcard incompatible with withCredentials), causing every auth POST to fail with a network error which surfaced as generic 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'. Fix: api.js compares window.location.origin to the env backend origin; if different, uses window.location.origin so requests are same-origin and cookies flow correctly. Verified on both hostnames.
